# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`), the terminal hand-off to child processes (the exec wrapper `internal/ui/teaexec`, use it instead of `tea.ExecProcess`, D121) and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci`, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface` |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage`, `internal/ui/datatable`, and the activity indicator column (`internal/ui/indicator`, `datatable.IndicatorColumn`, the row sentences `components.DescribeRow`) |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

## Implementation Plans

- **Location**: Always write implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` in the current project directory.
- **Format**: Use Markdown format for plans.
- **Naming**: Use descriptive names like `feature-name-plan.md` or `YYYY-MM-DD-feature-name.md`.

## Antigravity IDE Integration

When using the Antigravity IDE extension:
- Save all implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` relative to the project root.
- Create the directory if it doesn't exist before saving plans.
- Plans should be accessible from both Claude Code CLI and Antigravity IDE.

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner, viewport)

- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline

- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)

- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist

- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash

mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

# Cartographie réseau (vue Network) — brief

Statut : exploration (étape 1), à confronter.

## Idée en une phrase

Dans la vue Network, afficher une carte schématique de la topologie réseau (machine, passerelle, routeurs, devices du LAN, réseaux virtuels Docker/Podman/VM) et y suivre le chemin d'un appel réseau, saut après saut.

## Pour qui / problème

- Utilisateur : un dev/devops qui travaille chez lui ou en entreprise, avec des conteneurs et des VM sur sa machine.
- Question posée : « par où passe mon appel ? Pourquoi un appel depuis mon conteneur n'atteint-il pas sa cible ? »
- Aujourd'hui : `traceroute`, `mtr`, `ip route`, `docker network inspect`, et la vue netdiag de DevDesk (stage `route` : interface, source, passerelle).
- Ce qui manque : une vue unique qui relie conteneurs, bridges virtuels, interface, passerelle et sauts.

## Décisions prises avec l'utilisateur

- Besoin : les deux (vue d'ensemble **et** chemin d'un appel), le chemin d'un appel comme point d'entrée.
- Découverte **100 % automatique** (pas de description manuelle de la topologie).
- Rendu : **schéma en caractères (box-drawing) dans la TUI**, navigable au clavier. Pas d'export SVG/HTML.
- **Multiplateforme, sans dépendance externe** : pas de `traceroute`, `mtr`, `virsh` ou `VBoxManage`.
- Découpage en deux temps, accepté :
  1. Carte locale (pas de spike) : machine, interfaces, passerelle, réseaux Docker/Podman et conteneurs, bridges virtuels, voisins du LAN.
  2. Chemin d'un appel : cible saisie, parcours en surbrillance. Conditionné à un **spike** de faisabilité du trace natif par OS.
- Succès visé pour la première version : **voir d'un coup d'œil ce qui est branché** (vue d'ensemble de la topologie locale). Le chemin d'un appel suit en phase 2.

## Contraintes issues du projet

- `docs/architecture/network.md` : l'ancienne tab Topology (§3.44) et le route trace (§3.47) ont été **supprimés** parce qu'ils passaient par des conteneurs `--network host` et répondaient pour la mauvaise machine. Principe retenu : DevDesk ne prétend jamais répondre pour une machine qui n'est pas la sienne.
- Un trace natif avait trois inconnues non mesurées : ICMP `TIME_EXCEEDED` sans socket brut sur trois OS, TTL par paquet (`pro-bing` ne l'expose pas), mode TCP.
- Pistes sans privilège à mesurer : Linux (UDP + `IP_RECVERR`), Windows (`IcmpSendEcho`, TTL réglable), macOS (ICMP datagram, comportement à vérifier).
- Existant réutilisable : `internal/netiface`, `go-netroute`, `internal/docker` (réseaux, conteneurs), stage `route` de `internal/netcheck`.

## Limites assumées

- Switchs invisibles en L2 (sauf LLDP/CDP/SNMP, rares).
- Devices du LAN : IP, MAC, fabricant via ARP/NDP et mDNS/SSDP, sans savoir sur quel switch ils sont branchés.
- VM : bridges et interfaces virtuels seulement, pas le nom ni l'état des VM. Détail complet uniquement pour Docker/Podman.
- Un routeur qui filtre l'ICMP apparaît comme un saut `* * *`.

## Questions ouvertes

- OS ciblés précisément (Linux seul ou aussi macOS/Windows pour le MVP) : non tranché.
- Découverte du LAN : niveau d'intrusivité acceptable (scan actif ou seulement table de voisins).
- Place dans la vue Network : nouvelle tab ou vue dédiée.

systemPrompt:
Tu fais de la recherche documentaire pour éclairer une décision produit. Tu rapportes
des faits sourcés, pas des opinions.

## Méthode

1. Reformule la question de recherche et ce qui permettrait d'y répondre.
2. Cherche : produits concurrents et alternatives (y compris non logicielles et
   « ne rien faire »), discussions d'utilisateurs (forums, avis, issues), données de
   marché, réglementation applicable.
3. Pour chaque concurrent : cible, proposition de valeur, prix, forces, faiblesses
   observées par les utilisateurs.
4. Distingue fait sourcé, estimation et absence de donnée.

## Sortie

Synthèse en cinq points au plus, puis tableau des alternatives, puis preuves pour et
contre l'existence du problème, puis sources (URL + date de consultation). Si demandé,
écris le rapport dans `docs/product/<idée>/research.md`.

## Ne rien supposer

Ne comble jamais un manque de donnée par une estimation non signalée : écris « pas de
donnée trouvée ». Si la question de recherche est ambiguë au point de changer ce qu'il
faut chercher, rends d'abord la question à l'orchestrateur, avec ta reformulation
recommandée.

The search didn't turn up a specific GitHub issue requesting this feature. It did surface several open-source tools that already visualize Docker container networks, which may be useful if you're looking for an existing project or want to file a feature request on one of them.

- **Atlas** (github.com/karam-ajaj/atlas) is an MIT-licensed tool that maps containers, their IPs, ports, and network names in one dashboard, with circular or hierarchical layouts. It combines Go scanning backends, a FastAPI service, and a React dashboard to map infrastructure topology across subnets.
- **Port Navigator** (github.com/oslabs-beta/port-navigator) is a Docker extension that manages networks and ports. It can visualize your networks and containers in an Arc, Force, or Sankey display.
- **DockGraph** (github.com/dockgraph/dockgraph) connects to the Docker socket and shows your running environment as a live interactive topology map. Its author notes that containers are grouped by network, depends_on relationships appear as edges, and named volumes are linked to the containers that mount them.
- **Docker Network Graph** (hub.docker.com/r/leoverto/docker-network-graph) renders the relationship between networks and containers as a Graphviz graph. A fork by MuratovAS adds host connections and port visualization.
- **Wiremap** (github.com/codeofmario/wiremap) is an MIT-licensed explorer offering an interactive graph of containers grouped by network.
- **Weave Scope** shows containers as nodes, with lines between containers that communicate. Its API exposes the container topology.

Note that the Docker socket gives administrative access to the host, so some of these tools may need careful deployment. One review noted that in this version of the tool at least, there is no authentication to get into the interface.

Trippy's unprivileged mode lets you run traces without root or administrator rights, but it does not work on Windows, and its Linux and macOS support depends on the version.

- **Windows:** Unprivileged mode is not available there, because Windows lacks the ICMP socket type it needs. Unprivileged mode is not supported on NetBSD, FreeBSD or Windows as these platforms do not support the IPPROTO_ICMP socket type. Windows builds of Trippy need Administrator rights. Trippy must be run with Administrator privileges on Windows.
- **macOS and Linux:** Older release notes (0.11.0) say unprivileged mode is currently only supported on macOS. The same listing adds that Linux support is possible and may be added in the future. Newer documentation describes the mode as available on supported platforms only, and the Snap package lists it as a feature with Capabilities aware application (Linux only). I found no source that settles whether Linux is fully supported in the latest release, so check the current release notes.
- **Usage:** You enable it with the --unprivileged (-u) command line flag or by adding the unprivileged entry in the trippy section of the configuration file.
- **Limitation:** The paris and dublin ECMP strategies are not supported in unprivileged mode as these require manipulating the UDP and IP headers which in turn requires the use of a raw socket.
- **Background:** Trippy combines the functionality of traceroute and ping and is designed to assist with the analysis of networking issues.

**Unprivileged options:**
- **troute** (github.com/Wa4h1h/troute) is a Go traceroute implementation. Its TODO list notes that UDP tracing does not require root, while ICMP and TCP tracing do. The repo is archived, though: it was archived by its owner on Sep 9, 2024 and is now read-only.
- **go-traceroute** (github.com/kjansson/go-traceroute) is a minimalistic library for running UDP route tracing both synchronously and asynchronously. The results don't say whether it needs root, so check its docs before relying on it.
- **viaduct** (github.com/tonhe/viaduct) is a terminal traceroute replacement with ECMP multipath discovery. Its docs note that Linux users can avoid sudo by granting raw socket capability once. That's a capability grant, not a fully unprivileged mode.

**Privileged (raw sockets, need root or sudo):**
- **archer-v/gotraceroute** uses BPF (Berkley packet filter) connected to the socket in order to filter network packets at the kernel side, and its CLI is run with sudo. Its README also says BPF isn't supported on Windows and is not tested on Mac.
- **0ne-zero/traceroute** is a flexible, cross-platform traceroute library and CLI tool written in Go. Supports IPv4 & IPv6, and works on Linux, macOS, and Windows. It also notes that on Linux and macOS, raw sockets require sudo.
- **adakailabs/go-traceroute** lists Reusable and Concurrent raw IP socket (needs root) among its features.

Other results (zartbot/ztrace, pixelbender/go-traceroute, nirdosh17/tracer, denizydmr07/gotr, kanocz/tracelib) didn't say anything about privileges in the snippets I saw.

The most promising lead for an unprivileged, pure-Go tool is troute's UDP mode, but it's archived. If you need a maintained library, check go-traceroute's documentation to confirm whether its UDP mode needs root.

The search turned up a few relevant points, though nothing directly confirmed the IP_RECVTTL part of your query.

- **Error queue is the unprivileged mechanism.** The Linux-specific traceroute implementation says it relies on MSG_ERRQUEUE, which lets unprivileged users (no setuid bit) run some kinds of traceroute. It utilizes some currently Linux-specific features (including MSG_ERRQUEUE for recvmsg(2)), which allow such things like the use by unprivileged users (without setuid bit) for some type of tracerouting.
- **IP_RECVERR implementation example.** The ftr project's Linux socket module enables IP_RECVERR with setsockopt, then reads the control messages to find IP_RECVERR data and parses the extended error struct. Its ICMP origin check uses SO_EE_ORIGIN_ICMP. use crate::socket::icmp; is the module that handles the ICMP side. ftr's documentation says the kernel delivers ICMP Time Exceeded and Destination Unreachable messages via the error queue.
- **Port choice matters.** ftr uses port 443 in UDP mode, reasoning that it is less likely to be filtered by routers and firewalls. Its notes also say that Linux may drop or ignore ICMP Time Exceeded for UDP to uncommon high ports, which is the traditional 33434+ range.
- **ICMP without root is a separate path.** Unprivileged ICMP traceroute uses a SOCK_DGRAM IPPROTO_ICMP socket. A kernel 6.1.6 regression on Arch Linux broke this for non-root users, and a netdev thread linked it to IP_RECVERR handling, though that was a suspected bug in a traceroute binary, not a confirmed kernel fault. After upgrading from kernel 6.0.7 to 6.1.6 on Arch Linux, unprivileged ICMP traceroute using the traceroute -I tool stopped working.
- **Not covered.** None of the results discussed IP_RECVTTL, so I can't confirm its role in recovering the TTL of the ICMP reply, and a follow-up search would be needed for that.

The page covers IP_RECVERR but doesn't mention IP_RECVTTL, and it gives no numeric limits such as timeouts or rate caps.

**How it works (per the page)**
- UDP mode sends probes to port 443 instead of the traditional 33434+ range, which the page says is less likely to be filtered.
- It uses IP_RECVERR, which lets ftr receive ICMP errors without root. The page describes this as "No root privileges required on Linux (uses IP_RECVERR)."
- The kernel delivers ICMP Time Exceeded and Destination Unreachable messages through the socket's error queue. ftr parses them to identify the responding routers and the destination.
- Each probe carries an incrementing TTL, and routers that decrement it to zero are expected to reply with Time Exceeded.

**Caveats**
- Port 443 is less likely to be filtered, but that isn't guaranteed. Some networks still block or ignore UDP probes.
- Routers that ignore probes produce silent hops, so paths can look incomplete.
- Port selection is automatic in ftr, but system `traceroute -U` needs `-p 443` set manually to get the same benefit.
- ICMP mode is the alternative for better router responses, though it may need root depending on system configuration.

The search gives the documented intent of macOS unprivileged ICMP sockets, but it doesn't settle the specific "time exceeded not delivered" behavior you asked about.

- **Documented purpose:** Apple's ICMP man page says ICMP sockets can be opened with the SOCK_DGRAM socket type without requiring root privileges. It lists their uses as sending echo requests, receiving destination unreachable messages for path MTU discovery, and receiving time exceeded messages for traceroute (the synopsis is socket AF_INET SOCK_DGRAM IPPROTO_IP, per the man page's own text). The man page also says datagram ICMP sockets offer a subset of the functionality available to raw ICMP sockets.
- **Reported problems:** An Apple Developer Forums thread titled "ICMP reply not received" describes a DGRAM-based program where select() times out either way, which suggests replies can go missing even with the unprivileged socket. I could not confirm the cause from the snippet.
- **Possible explanation:** A third-party guide notes that some networks block these reports, which can make traceroute misleading. That points to network filtering as one cause, though it's a general observation rather than a macOS-specific finding.
- **Working example:** A ping3 user reports that a SOCK_DGRAM/IPPROTO_ICMP socket works for pinging on macOS without root (I can demonstrate this on my macOS system), and a docs.rs crate notes that on macOS, both RAW and DGRAM sockets include IP headers, which matters when parsing received packets.

Gap: none of the results document a macOS bug or limitation where DGRAM sockets fail to deliver Time Exceeded messages. A more targeted search (for example, the Apple forum thread's full discussion or XNU source for ICMP datagram sockets) would be needed to confirm that.

The go-graph-layout module is a Go library for graph layout that includes a Sugiyama-style layered layout, though it is still a work in progress.

- **Scope:** The README says it aims to implement graph visualization algorithms from scratch in Go instead of binding to Graphviz. It is work in progress.
- **Sugiyama support:** The feature list includes a Kozo Sugiyama layers strategy, and the layout package documents a phased breakdown of layered graph construction. Its layout types include a Sugiyama layers strategy layout and a Brandes-Köpf horizontal coordinate assigner.
- **Incomplete parts:** The README marks Brandes-Köpf horizontal layer assignment and the Graphviz dot layers algorithm as 80% done.
- **Versions:** v0.0.1 was published May 9, 2024 under MIT. A v0.2.0 layout package page from Dec 11, 2024 shows a warning that it is not in the latest version of its module, so newer releases may exist. I could not confirm the current latest version from these results.
- **Adoption:** An ecosyste.ms listing reports 70 stars on GitHub and no forks, which suggests a small user base.

- **Linux:** The library tries an unprivileged ping by default, using a datagram ICMP socket rather than a raw socket. This requires the `net.ipv4.ping_group_range` sysctl to be enabled. Alternatively, you can call `pinger.SetPrivileged(true)` and grant the binary `cap_net_raw` with setcap, or run it as root.
- **Windows:** You must call `pinger.SetPrivileged(true)`, or you get a socket error. The README says this should not require elevated privileges, and it was tested on Windows 10.
- **macOS:** The page doesn't mention macOS.

- **Setting TTL:** The page doesn't describe a method for setting TTL. It only covers `SetMark` (Linux `SO_MARK`) and `SetDoNotFragment` (Linux).

content.content:
## Privilege Requirements by OS

**Linux (Unix section)**
- **Run via `sudo`:** `sudo trip example.com`. The config file must be reachable by the root user, or you must pass it with `-c`.
- **Set the setuid bit:** `chown` `trip` to root and run `chmod +s`.
- **Set capabilities:** `sudo setcap CAP_NET_RAW+p $(which trip)`. This is Linux-only.
- **Required capability:** `CAP_NET_RAW`. Trippy drops all capabilities after creating the raw sockets.
- **Unprivileged mode:** Not supported. The page says Linux support "may be added in the future."

**macOS (Unix section)**
- **Run via `sudo`** and **setuid bit** are both listed for Unix. The page does not mention macOS-specific steps.
- **Set capabilities** does not apply, since it is Linux-only.
- **Unprivileged mode:** Supported. It is currently the only platform where it is.

**Windows**
- "Trippy must be run with Administrator privileges on Windows."
- No sudo, setuid, or capability options are listed.
- **Unprivileged mode:** Not supported.

## Unprivileged Mode

- **Enable:** Use the `--unprivileged` (`-u`) flag, or set `unprivileged = true` in the `[trippy]` section of the config file.
- **Tracing modes:** Works for ICMP, UDP, and TCP.
- **Platform support:** Currently macOS only. Not supported on NetBSD, FreeBSD, or Windows, which lack the `IPPROTO_ICMP` socket type.
- **Limitation:** The `paris` and `dublin` ECMP strategies are not supported. They need raw socket access to manipulate UDP and IP headers.

- **Enable:** Use the `--unprivileged` (`-u`) flag, or set `unprivileged = true` in the `[trippy]` section of the config file.
- **Tracing modes:** Works for ICMP, UDP, and TCP.
- **Platform support:** Currently macOS only. Not supported on NetBSD, FreeBSD, or Windows, which lack the `IPPROTO_ICMP` socket type.
- **Limitation:** The `paris` and `dublin` ECMP strategies are not supported. They need raw socket access to manipulate UDP and IP headers.
